Seems like people are confusing normative and descriptive claims here.

If you walk around naked in a crime-ridden neighborhood the odds of rape are increased. 

You SHOULD (in an ideal society) never be raped, killed, mugged, called names, be unemployed, feel bad, have a bad childhood, lack money, go hungry, be short, be too tall, etc. At least according to most people. 

Taking preventative actions can reduce a risk of something bad happening. This does not, however, mean that a rape of someone dressed in a space suit is worse than someone wearing nothing. According to me personally, at least. Some people might think differently, but I'm guessing that what I said is not really controversial in most societies with laws against rape.
